summary: Durable multi-agent purchase order approval demo. Temporal orchestrates a LangGraph extraction agent (Bedrock-backed), a guardrail check, a human-in-the-loop approval step, and a simulated ERP submission, all triggerable from a browser UI.
background: Built for a PepsiCo showcase, requested during a Temporal design review call on Sep 2, 2026. PepsiCo asked for a medium to high complexity multi-agent workflow to demo internally ahead of their own hackathon (week of Sep 14), which certifies telemetry capture, human-in-the-loop, failure modes, and guardrails.
constraints: Model provider must be Amazon Bedrock via ChatBedrockConverse (langchain-aws), not a direct Anthropic or OpenAI API call.
Use the Temporal LangGraph plugin to run the extraction agent as a durable activity.
Human-in-the-loop must use a Temporal signal or update, not polling.
ERP submission retries must rely on Temporal's built-in activity retry behavior, not custom retry logic in the activity.
No PepsiCo-specific integration (Apigee, DevX, asset marketplace). This is a standalone demo repo.
No emojis, no em dashes, no unnecessary flashy formatting in any generated docs or README.

All Bedrock model calls must be real, live invocations against the actual Bedrock endpoint. Do not stub, mock, hardcode, or fake the LLM response anywhere in the demo, including during development iterations. If a test needs to run without live credentials, that test should be skipped, not backed by a fake response.

stories.title: Project scaffold
stories.description: Set up repo structure separating workflow code, activity code, and the UI/API layer. Include a README stub.
acceptanceCriteria: Repo has clear top-level folders for workflows, activities, api, and ui
README explains how to run the worker and the UI locally

stories.title: Bedrock access check
stories.description: Verify Bedrock model access is granted for the target Claude model under the configured AWS account before building against it, using the Agent Toolkit for AWS.
acceptanceCriteria: A simple script or check confirms the target Bedrock model is invokable with current credentials
Failure produces a clear error message, not a silent hang

stories.title: Orchestrator workflow skeleton
stories.description: Implement the Temporal workflow (Python SDK) that will coordinate the PO approval process: extraction, guardrail check, optional human approval, ERP submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow accepts a PO payload and runs to completion on a trivial happy-path input
Workflow is visible and inspectable in the local Temporal Web UI

stories.title: Extraction agent (LangGraph + Bedrock)
stories.description: Build the LangGraph extraction agent, run as a Temporal activity via the LangGraph plugin, using ChatBedrockConverse as the model client. It should parse a PO payload into structured fields (amount, vendor, requester, line items).
acceptanceCriteria: Agent runs as a Temporal activity, not a plain function call
Model calls go through Bedrock and are visible as such in logs
Structured output is returned to the workflow
The Bedrock call is real and live in every run and every demo scenario, never mocked or hardcoded

stories.title: Guardrail check step
stories.description: Implement a deterministic guardrail check activity that flags a PO as over policy if it exceeds a configurable spending threshold.
acceptanceCriteria: Threshold is configurable via env var or config file
Workflow branches based on the guardrail result

stories.title: Human-in-the-loop approval
stories.description: When a PO is flagged, pause the workflow and wait for an approve or reject decision delivered via a Temporal signal or update.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflow pauses cleanly and resumes on receiving the signal/update
Both approve and reject paths lead to a distinct, correct final workflow state

stories.title: ERP submission with seeded failure
stories.description: Implement a simulated ERP submission activity with a configurable seeded failure count, so the first N attempts fail and the next one succeeds, relying on Temporal's native retry policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Failure count is configurable
Temporal's built-in retry mechanism handles the retries without custom retry code in the activity
Retry attempts are visible in the Temporal Web UI

stories.title: API layer
stories.description: Build a thin API (FastAPI or equivalent) between the UI and the Temporal client, supporting workflow start, signal/update, and query calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Endpoints exist to start a PO workflow, send an approve/reject decision, and query current status
API errors are surfaced clearly, not swallowed

stories.title: UI: workflow diagram and scenario triggers
stories.description: Build the main UI pane: a visual diagram of the workflow that highlights the active step in real time, with buttons for each scenario (happy path, guardrail violation, human-in-the-loop, failure and retry).
acceptanceCriteria: All five scenarios listed in the summary are triggerable from the UI without a terminal
The diagram visibly updates as the workflow progresses, without manual refresh

stories.title: UI: telemetry/event feed
stories.description: Add a log or trace panel showing completed and in-progress steps with status and latency, driven by a Temporal query or lightweight event log.
acceptanceCriteria: Feed updates live during a workflow run
Each entry shows step name, status, and latency or timestamp

stories.title: UI stretch: synced code side panel
stories.description: Optional. Add a right-hand code viewer that auto-scrolls to and highlights the source file and function currently executing, staying in sync with the active workflow step.
acceptanceCriteria: Highlighted code matches the currently executing step without manual refresh
If this story is skipped, note the decision and reason in the README

stories.title: README and first-time run-through
stories.description: Write a README that lets a first-time viewer with no Temporal background run the demo end to end, covering setup, running the worker, running the UI, and walking through each scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: A person unfamiliar with the repo can follow the README and complete all five scenarios
README notes whether the code side panel (story 4.1) was built

openQuestions: Single HTML page vs small Next.js app for the UI? Default: simplest option that still supports story 4.1; fall back to a single page if 4.1 is dropped.
resolvedDecisions: The extraction agent's Bedrock call is real and live in every run, never mocked. The guardrail check itself stays deterministic (rule-based), but that's a separate step from whether the LLM call is real.
